english: For a real number $p>-1$, let $W(p)=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin^{p}x\,dx$. Then the value of $W\left(\dfrac52\right)W\left(\dfrac72\right)$ is ______.
hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $p>-1$ के लिए माना $W(p)=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin^{p}x\,dx$ है। तब $W\left(\dfrac52\right)W\left(\dfrac72\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: This is the Wallis relation $(n+1)W_nW_{n+1}=\frac{\pi}{2}$ extended to real $p$
solution_full: For non-integer $p$ Wallis' product formula does not apply directly; use the Gamma form of the same integral: $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^{p}x\,dx=\dfrac{\Gamma\left(\frac{p+1}{2}\right)\Gamma\left(\frac12\right)}{2\,\Gamma\left(\frac{p}{2}+1\right)}$, with $\Gamma\left(\frac12\right)=\sqrt\pi$.

For integer $p=n$ this is the familiar Wallis consequence $W_nW_{n+1}=\dfrac{\pi}{2(n+1)}$, which follows from the Wallis reduction $W_{n+2}=\frac{n+1}{n+2}W_n$; the same reduction holds for real $p$, and the Gamma form supplies the starting value.
With $p=\frac52$: $W\left(\frac52\right)W\left(\frac72\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{2\cdot\frac72}=\dfrac{\pi}{7}=0.4487\ldots$, which is $0.45$ to two decimal places.
originality_note: New: two Wallis-type integrals with half-integer exponents, neither elementary, whose product is elementary (pi/7) by the Gamma form (way 4). Closest known: the Wallis identity (n+1) W_n W_{n+1} = pi/2 for integer n (standard exercise). Different because: the exponents are fractional, so Wallis' formula alone fails and Gamma is needed.
blueprint_concepts: Gamma function as a shortcut for standard definite integrals

concept_use.Walli's theorem in Integration: The Wallis relation W_n W_{n+1} = pi/(2(n+1)) (from the reduction W_{n+2} = (n+1)/(n+2) W_n) is the pattern being extended to p = 5/2.
concept_use.Gamma function as a shortcut for standar: W(p) = Gamma((p+1)/2) sqrt(pi)/(2 Gamma(p/2 + 1)) evaluates the fractional-power integrals; Gamma(s+1) = s Gamma(s) collapses the product.

stem_review: Read as a student: W(p) is defined for p > -1 (convergent); product checked by quadrature: 0.448799 = pi/7. Answer 0.45 lies between 0 and 1 as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Write each integral in Gamma form; the Gamma values telescope to 2/(p+1).
justification: Routine for a student who knows the Gamma form: two substitutions into a formula and one cancellation. Above 2021-P2-Q11 (L1); L2.
